example_summary: Mr. Bhargava's professional fee of ₹ 5 lacs used for a self-created trust is taxable as application of income.
source_provision:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Diversion vs Application of Income

| Doctrine Aspect | Statutory Basis | Legal Condition & Benchmark | Tax Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Diversion of Income** | Section 4 / Section 5 | Creation of a prior charge by overriding title before the income reaches the assessee. | Excluded from the total income of the recipient. |
| **Application of Income** | Section 4 / Section 28 | Income reaches the assessee first as taxable receipts, and is voluntarily utilized thereafter. | Fully taxable under respective head of income. |
| **Professional Receipts** | Section 28(iv) | Fees received by a professional on condition of voluntary charity creation. | Assessed as Profits and Gains of Business or Profession. |



> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Judicial Precedent Benchmark**: The Supreme Court test dictates that where the obligation is self-imposed out of income already earned or received, it is merely an application of income. True diversion requires an overriding legal charge existing at the very source of receipt.



- **Source of Receipt**: Professional fees or remuneration received for services rendered vest entirely in the hands of the professional.
- **Voluntary Trust Creation**: Subsequent execution of a trust deed out of received sums represents personal discretion and application, not statutory exemption.

director.justification: The issue hinges on distinguishing whether the fee of ₹ 5 lacs received by Mr. Bhargava is an excludable Diversion of Income by overriding title or a taxable Application of Income under Section 28.
director.visual_metaphor: A dual-channel pipeline showing income diverted by an overriding legal gate prior to receipt versus income landing in the professional hand before voluntary outlay.

beat_plan.beat_goal: Introduce Mr. Bhargava defending a company in the Supreme Court on condition of receiving ₹ 5 lacs for creating a charitable trust.
Contrast the doctrine of Diversion of Income by overriding title against Application of Income.
Examine the source of obligation to determine if the client created an overriding legal charge before receipt.
Conclude that the amount is an application of professional income fully assessable under Section 28.

beats.voice_sync_text: ഇവിടെ നമ്മൾ Section 4-ഉം Section 5-ഉം പ്രകാരം Diversion of Income-ഉം Application of Income-ഉം തമ്മിലുള്ള വ്യത്യാസമാണ് പഠിക്കുന്നത്. Income ഒരു assessee-യുടെ കൈകളിൽ എത്തുന്നതിന് മുൻപ് തന്നെ ആ തുകയ്ക്ക്മേൽ legal charge ഉണ്ടെങ്കിൽ അത് diversion ആകുന്നു. എന്നാൽ തുക കിട്ടിയതിനു ശേഷം voluntary ആയി apply ചെയ്താൽ അത് application of income ആണ്.
beats.director_goal: Contrast the doctrine of Diversion of Income by overriding title against Application of Income.

beats.voice_sync_text: Income generate ചെയ്യുന്ന source-ൽ തന്നെ വേറൊരു ആൾക്ക് legal right അല്ലെങ്കിൽ overriding title ഉണ്ടെങ്കിൽ, ആ തുക assessee-യുടെ income ആയി കണക്കാക്കാൻ പറ്റില്ല. എന്നാൽ ഇവിടെ Mr. Bhargava സ്വയം ഉണ്ടാക്കിയ self-imposed obligation ആയതിനാൽ ഇത് അദ്ദേഹത്തിന്റെ professional income തന്നെയാണ്.

beats.voice_sync_text: Professional fees ആയി ലഭിക്കുന്ന തുക എപ്പോഴും Section 28 പ്രകാരം Profits and gains of business or profession എന്ന head-ൽ ആണ് charge ചെയ്യപ്പെടുന്നത്. അതുകൊണ്ട് ഈ ₹ 5 lacs പൂർണ്ണമായും taxable ആണ്. തുക കിട്ടിയ ശേഷം ആര് trust ഉണ്ടാക്കി എന്നതുകൊണ്ട് professional income-ന്റെ taxability മാറില്ല.
